headline: Committee reviews farm, water, environment, ferry and bus programs

meeting.body: Maui County Council Agriculture, Diversification, Environment, & Public Transportation Committee
meeting.voteItem: Designating the ferry operator's president as a resource person
meeting.summary: Committee reviews farm, water, environment, ferry and bus programs.
meeting.recap: A Kula watershed group asked for more County funding to protect watersheds after wildfires.[[0:36:19]] The Department of Agriculture said its budget is $8,312,316, a temporary 3% drop from the fiscal year 24 budget.[[1:15:14]] The department said it gave grants to about 64 of 111 applicants, up from 22 last year.[[1:19:23]] The department said a County food and nutrition security plan should be finalized in the next week or two.[[1:22:09]] EP&S said its green grants program grew from $160,000 to $5.86 million.[[2:52:29]] A County ferry study looked at service linking Maui, Molokaʻi and Lānaʻi without carrying vehicles.[[3:19:06]] The consultant estimated a yearly operating subsidy of $1.8 million to $1.9 million.[[3:52:47]]
decided: The committee, with no objections, named the ferry operator's president as a resource person under Rule 18A.
The committee deferred the ferry feasibility study item with no objections.
meeting.next: A council member asked staff to follow up on the Kula Ag Park funding distribution. The consultant said the first step for a County ferry would be an environmental assessment (a formal environmental review). The environmental assessment was estimated to take about a year.

moments.q: "We need a drop-off center really bad."

issues.oneLine: A Kula watershed group asked for County funding to restore land burned in the Kula fire.
issues.why: The testifier said the 2023 fire left degraded soil, more erosion risk, and land that holds less water.
issues.brief: The group said it has received zero County funding.[[#1]] The testifier said federal funding for recovery and mitigation is decreasing or ending.[[#2]] A biochar company said it needs funding to keep providing free biochar to fire survivors and damaged properties.[[#3]]
